title: Entries of a matching monomial
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $\sigma$ be a permutation of the set $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. Define a monomial by summing, over all indices $i$, the exponent vector that assigns exponent $1$ to the variable indexed by $(i,\sigma(i))$ and $0$ to all other variables. At a variable indexed by $(a,b)$, its exponent is $1$ if $\sigma(a)=b$ and $0$ otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: $\sigma$ is a permutation of the indices from $0$ to $n-1$
